question.text: Which of the following best describes the 'Liquidation Period' under Regulation 29(9A)?

answer.text: A 2-year period before scheme launch for capital-raising
A 1-year period following expiry of tenure (or extended tenure) of the AIF scheme, for fully liquidating scheme assets
A perpetual period with unlimited extension
A 6-month period immediately after scheme launch

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 13.5: The 'Liquidation Period' is a period of 1 YEAR following the expiry of tenure or EXTENDED tenure of the AIF scheme, for fully liquidating the assets. Where assets cannot be liquidated, in-specie distribution or Dissolution Period (75% consent) is triggered. **The Trap:** Options A, C, D invert purpose or timing. The 1-year post-tenure definition is crisp in the PDF. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C/D test the same Liquidation Period definition. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Line up buyers/valuers/merchant-bankers on Year-0 of Liquidation Period — 12 months vanish quickly against illiquid marks. If the first 6 months show no traction, start Dissolution Period paperwork immediately.
